//requiredFirstLoad: The INVERSE of the budget, and of the ratchet P6 adds. Everywhere else this file asks 'has the tracked module stayed OUT of this route's first-load graph'. Here it asks the opposite: client.ts sets detectSessionInUrl:true, so auth-js parses the magic-link fragment at CONSTRUCTION, and the auth path needs that construction to happen during initial module evaluation -- before hydration, before the router can rewrite the URL. Deferring it there loses a real user's session silently and tells them their link expired. Until P5 that edge existed only by ACCIDENT (AuthGuard.tsx and ListingRequestForm.tsx were merely unconverted), so the arc's own remaining work would have removed it with nothing failing. src/integrations/supabase/eagerAuthClient.ts makes it intentional; this makes it enforced. BLOCKING, unlike the report-only attribution above: a missing required edge exits 1.

requiredFirstLoad.why: detectSessionInUrl parses the magic-link fragment at client construction; the auth path must construct eagerly, not behind getSupabase(). Held by src/integrations/supabase/eagerAuthClient.ts.

//pullerRatchet: P6, the arc's closing guard. P0 built the puller count as an INSTRUMENT -- it printed, nothing enforced -- which was right while the number was still moving: home was being driven 3 -> 0 and a guard pinned to a number you are about to change is noise. The number has stopped moving, so it becomes a contract. WHY A RATCHET AND NOT A BUDGET: the KB budget cannot catch this class, and P5 proved it -- simulating the regression left the auth route at 233.6 KB against a 310 budget, so the defect read as a 43.8 KB WIN. Weight and graph membership are different questions and only one of them is what this arc bought. BOTH DIRECTIONS BLOCK. Over the allowance is a regression: vendor-supabase has re-entered a graph six phases removed it from, and the puller + module-edge lists printed by the guard name the exact import to route through getSupabase(). UNDER the allowance also fails, because an allowance nobody tightens stops describing the code -- it decays into a ceiling with slack and the next regression hides in the slack; the fix is a one-line edit in the PR that earned the win, which is when the number is best understood. Every budgeted route must have an entry: a budgeted route with no ratchet can take on unlimited pullers silently. home 0 is the arc's completion proof and the row that must never rise. event 2 and auth 2 are pins, not targets -- auth's edge is REQUIRED (see requiredFirstLoad above), so its allowance can never honestly reach 0. event was 3 until 2026-08-14, when P1 of the vendor-cost arc moved tslib out of vendor-supabase (it rides with vendor-react -- see the tslib branch in vite.config.ts, which explains why it is not a chunk of its own) and the third puller vanished. That puller was never real in the sense the ratchet means: tslib is a shared helper runtime that happens to be installed as a Supabase dependency, so rollup filed it inside vendor-supabase and any chunk compiled with tslib helpers acquired a static edge to the 43 KB Supabase client to reach three one-line functions. The ratchet counted that edge honestly -- the chunk really did import vendor-supabase -- which is exactly why the row is a MEASUREMENT and not a judgement, and why it went UNDER and refused to pass until the win was written down.
//chunkRatchet: The SSR ROUTES' first-load request gate, enforced by scripts/check-bundle-budget.mjs. Added 2026-08-15 by PR 3 of the vendor-cost arc. firstLoadRequestRatchet below counts requests exactly, by parsing prerendered HTML -- but only PRERENDERED routes have a document on disk, and /city/:slug and /event/:id are on-demand SSR and emit none. Those two are the highest-traffic pages in the app and most of the edge-request bill this arc exists to cut, and until this block existed NOTHING blocked on their first-load request count. This closes the hole from the other side: the vite manifest graph already yields a first-load JS CHUNK count for every budgeted route, SSR included, and that number has been measured, stored in attribution.baseline and diffed on every run since P0 -- REPORT-ONLY, gating nothing. Turning it into a contract is the entire change; the measurement is untouched. WHY THE KB BUDGETS CANNOT STAND IN: splitting one 40 KB chunk into forty 1 KB chunks costs 39 extra requests on every view and approximately zero bytes, so every maxFirstLoadGzipKB above would report that as a small WIN. A CHUNK COUNT IS NOT A REQUEST COUNT, said here rather than left to be discovered from a number that looks low: it omits the stylesheet and the document itself, and on an SSR route it cannot see anything the server adds to the HTML. What makes it a defensible proxy rather than a guess is the cross-check available on the six PRERENDERED routes, where both numbers exist and are produced by two guards reading two DIFFERENT artefacts -- every firstLoadRequestRatchet pin below is exactly the chunk pin here plus one stylesheet (51 = 50 + 1, 33 = 32 + 1). BOTH EDGES BLOCK, as pullerRatchet and firstLoadRequestRatchet do and for the same reason: an allowance nobody tightens decays into a ceiling with slack, and the next regression hides inside the slack. EVERY BUDGETED ROUTE MUST HAVE AN ENTRY, the assertion pullerRatchet already carries -- a budgeted route with no chunk entry can be split into unlimited requests without a word. ALLOWANCES ARE POSITIVE INTEGERS, where pullerRatchet's floor is 0: zero pullers is a real and desirable state (home's 0 is the defer arc's completion proof), but no route loads zero chunks -- one resolving to zero fails assertMeasured first -- so a 0 here could only be a typo, and it would sit permanently red while LOOKING like a pin. MEASURED IN CI at bcc81b1, the tree that merged as ebfa2c1, and independently reproduced by a clean local Windows build: the two agree EXACTLY on all eight chunk counts, unlike the KB figures, which do not (see the baseline note below). That platform-independence is what makes these safe to BLOCK on rather than merely report. TIGHTENED 2026-09-04: event 52 -> 51, claimed by the series-termination arc's W17 pass. BentoPage stopped importing useSeo/buildSeoForRoute -- a call that had been INERT since S4 (a framework route that renders a page sets RouteOwnsHeadContext and useSeo returns before touching the head), so the buildSeoForRoute chunk left /event/:id's first-load graph with no behaviour change at all. NAMING THE CHUNK EXACTLY, because the first draft of this note said "the seo module" left and a review walked the manifest: only assets/buildSeoForRoute-*.js went. assets/useSeo-*.js is STILL on every /event/:id first load -- BentoPage keeps importing SITE_ORIGIN from @/lib/seo, which re-exports it from useSeo.ts -- so it remains a candidate for the next engineer shedding chunks here, not a win already banked. The delta is otherwise clean: the rendered head is byte-identical to prod on an ended event, a live festival and a festival served at /event/<slug>. //firstLoadRequestRatchet: The REQUEST-COUNT contract, enforced by scripts/check-first-load-requests.mjs (npm run check:first-load-requests, after npm run build). Everything else in this file counts BYTES; this counts DOCUMENTS FETCHED, and they are not the same question. Splitting one 40 KB chunk into forty 1 KB chunks is free in bytes and costs 39 requests on every view -- every KB budget above would report that as a small win. It exists because Vercel meters edge REQUESTS and this account measured 1.8M against a 1M allowance (180%) on 2026-08-14 while sitting at 33% of its byte allowance: ~18 KB per request, so COUNT was the entire lever and weight was never the problem. WHAT THE NUMBER IS: per prerendered index.html, the union of every modulepreload href, the stylesheet, any preload with as=script or as=style, and the static import specifiers inside the inline module script. A union rather than a tag count because React Router bootstraps the route through an inline `import * as route0 from ...`, a real request no tag count would ever see. Deliberately EXCLUDED, so a low number is not mistaken for the whole waterfall: the document itself, favicons, the manifest, preconnect hints, and the font preload -- the guard prints that one per route instead of hiding it. Measured at d89f92b and CORROBORATED INDEPENDENTLY: check-bundle-budget.mjs walks the vite manifest graph and reports 50 / 50 / 32 JS chunks for parties / classes / faq, which is exactly these pins minus the one stylesheet each. Two methods reading two different artefacts and agreeing is why these are pinned rather than sampled. BOTH EDGES BLOCK, exactly as pullerRatchet above: over is a regression, and UNDER fails too, because an allowance nobody tightens decays into a ceiling with slack and the next regression hides in the slack -- tighten it in the PR that earned the win, which is when the number is best understood. COVERAGE IS COMPUTED FROM THE ARTEFACT, not from this list: every index.html under build/client must have a pin and every pin must still name a prerendered route. Add a route to react-router.config.ts prerender without a pin and the guard fails, rather than the new page shipping unwatched -- which is why the three all-prose landing pages sit here beside the three routes the arc targets. They were measured, not assumed, and they are all 33. WHAT THIS DOES NOT COVER, stated here as well as in the guard because a green run is otherwise easy to over-read: only PRERENDERED routes have a document to count, so /city/:slug and /event/:id -- the highest-traffic pages, and most of the request bill this exists to control -- are structurally outside it. They are on-demand SSR + ISR and emit no HTML at build time. What covers them instead is chunkRatchet ABOVE, which gates a first-load JS CHUNK count for every budgeted route, SSR included, and blocks on both edges. That was report-only until PR 3 of the vendor-cost arc on 2026-08-15; the sentence here used to end 'and those are report-only', which stopped being true in the commit that added the block. A chunk count is not a request count, so the two are not interchangeable -- see the chunkRatchet note for what it does and does not see. NOTE THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN THE TWO BLOCKS, because nothing enforces it: on these six routes each pin here is exactly its chunkRatchet pin plus one stylesheet. If you move one, check the other, or the cross-check that justifies the proxy quietly stops being a cross-check while both guards stay green.

attribution.//trackedChunkName: Matched against the manifest node's chunk `name`, i.e. the manualChunks group key in vite.config.ts -- NOT the hashed filename, which changes on every content edit. If that group is ever renamed the guard hard-fails rather than reporting a reassuring 0: a tracker that silently measures nothing is the failure mode rule R1 of check-script-conventions.mjs exists to catch.
attribution.//trackedModule: The first-party module that leads INTO trackedChunkName, and the target of the module-level edge report. A chunk name cannot serve: no import statement names a chunk, so the chunk-level puller list can say where the weight is but never which import to delete. That gap is why 'is this the last edge?' was answered by `grep -rl integrations/supabase/client` three times and was wrong three times -- grep sees direct importers of a string, not a barrel re-export (@/lib/seo -> useEntitySlugOrId), a provider three components deep (root -> SearchProvider -> SearchOverlay -> searchClickTelemetry), or a loader helper (home -> detailLoader -> resolvePublicEventRef). All three misses were of exactly those shapes, and two of them were recorded in the arc plan as out of scope on the strength of a grep. If this module stops being the way in (client.ts retired, or the client constructed somewhere else), repoint it -- the guard hard-fails if the path is not a file, rather than reporting 0 edges for every route.

PR 2's row was measured on a local Windows box. Its first CI run then reported every one of the eight routes 0.2-0.4 KB LIGHTER: home -0.2, event -0.4, auth -0.3, parties -0.3, classes -0.3, faq -0.2, both landing rows -0.2. Systematic, all eight, always negative, and NOT drift -- chunk counts, puller counts and request counts were byte-identical across the two runs, and every gate passed. THE CAUSE IS BUILD-TIME ENV INLINING, and the first draft of this note got it wrong in a way worth recording. It said 'Linux/LF against Windows/CRLF in the bundled source'. That is DISPROVEN: .gitattributes line 5 is `* text=auto eol=crlf`, committed months before either run, and `git ls-files --eol` reports `attr/text=auto eol=crlf` on the source, so CI's ubuntu checkout produces CRLF too and both builds see byte-identical inputs. The real mechanism is that Vite substitutes import.meta.env.VITE_* as string LITERALS at build time, so the LENGTH of the key lands in the bundle: perf-budget.yml injects a 125-char placeholder and defines no VITE_SUPABASE_PROJECT_ID, while a local build inlines .env's real 210-char key and a 22-char project id. MEASURED, not argued: rebuilding locally with CI's exact placeholder moved every route to within 0.1 KB of the CI figures below, from 0.2-0.4 KB out, and the placeholder is grep-able in four built chunks. A uniform 0.1 KB residual remains -- most likely the project id, which is inlined into one chunk that every route loads -- and is NOT separately verified; do not treat that last 0.1 as explained. Report-only, so nothing reddened; but the baseline would have gone on printing a small negative delta on EVERY future CI run, and '-0.3 KB' reads as 'this PR saved 0.3 KB' -- a number meaning something other than what it says, which is the exact failure this block's own re-baselining rule exists to prevent. THE FIX IS TO MEASURE WHERE THE COMPARING HAPPENS: CI measures every future PR, so a local baseline is the one figure that cannot be reproduced by the thing doing the comparison. HOW TO REPRODUCE THESE NUMBERS LOCALLY, which is now possible and is the better answer than tolerating a delta: build with the env perf-budget.yml declares. `npm run pre-ship` already does exactly that -- its build:ship step reads that workflow's env rather than .env -- so a bare `npm run build` is the only path that will print a small POSITIVE delta here, around +0.2 to +0.4 KB. That delta is the env difference, not a regression, and it is not a licence to ignore a change in that band: re-measure with the CI env before concluding anything. Figures come from the bundle-budget job of PR #255's CI run, measured at bcc81b1, whose tree is identical to the squash merge ebfa2c1 named in the commit field -- verified with git diff, not assumed. NONE OF THIS TOUCHES THE CHUNK COLUMN: CI and a clean local build agree EXACTLY on all eight chunk counts, which is what made it safe for chunkRatchet above to block on them rather than merely report them.
